ops: There are 6 top tricks outside of diamonds (the @SA, 2 in hearts, and 3 in clubs).
South must hope to play diamonds for 5 tricks
and that East was dealt the @SK along with the heart length that he showed in the bidding.

If East has the @SK then it should be possible for South to come to a 12th trick through some sort of major suit squeeze. There are 2 losers, however, and no useful way to rectify the count down to the 1 loser that a ^*Bsimple squeeze^*N would require. South's only chance is to play for a 2-loser ^*Bstrip squeeze^*N, but it may be necessary to guess the distribution of East's hand in the end game.
After winning West's heart opening lead,
South should focus his attention on the diamond suit. With 3 cards missing it is correct to finesse West for the @DK.
South should be careful to start diamonds by leading the @DJ in case West was dealt all 3 outstanding cards in that suit.
On the actual layout the @DJ holds the trick as East follows suit.
South should continue by cashing all of his diamond and club winners, noting East's discards.
East discards 3 hearts and the @S10 on dummy's diamonds
and follows suit to 3 rounds of clubs.
South should cash the @HA to confirm the count in that suit
and West's discard means that hearts were 6-1 (as East's weak 2@H opening suggested).
South must now decide which defender was dealt the 13th club. If West has that card then East was dealt 3613 distribution and is down to 2 spades and 1 heart.
In this case South must exit in hearts to East
who will then be endplayed into leading away from the @SK.
If East was dealt the outstanding club (and 2614 distribution) then South will be sorry if he exits in hearts to East.
East will cash the 13th club to defeat the contract.
On this layout South must cash the @SA to drop East's @SK instead of exiting in hearts.
The defense has discarded well and South has no way of really knowing which defender was dealt the 13th club.

It can, however, be shown that West is more likely than East to hold that card. West is known to have been dealt 1 heart and 2 diamonds for a total of 3 known cards in those suits. East is known to have started with 6 hearts, 1 diamond, and the presumed @SK for a total of 8 known cards in those suits.
Therefore, West is a favorite to hold the 13th club as there are more "spaces" in his hand for that card.
South should exit in hearts at the critical point, hoping that East was dealt 3613 distribution and will be will be endplayed into leading away from the @SK.
The ^*Bstrip squeeze^*N aspect of this deal took place on the run of the diamonds and clubs. East was eventually forced to discard 3 potential heart winners.
It was then safe for South to throw East on lead in hearts without having to worry about him winning any more heart tricks.
^*BStrip squeezes^*N mature with 2 or more losers. These squeezes are very useful when it is impossible for the declarer to rectify the count down to the 1 loser that a ^*Bsimple squeeze^*N requires.

In this deal, for example, if South had tried to duck a spade or heart trick early in an attempt to rectify the count, he would have destroyed his threat card in the suit that he played. With only 1 threat suit remaining there would be no squeeze.
